title: AI Was Wrong 80% of the Time. They Followed It Anyway
description:
1,372 people. AI was wrong 80% of the time. They followed it anyway.

Cognitive surrender is real. Wharton researchers proved it. MIT confirmed it with brain scans. A Frontiers study of 589 people showed you cannot even tell it is happening to you.

In this video: six peer-reviewed mechanisms explaining what AI does to your brain — from cognitive offloading to the Generative Capacity Erosion Hypothesis. All from 2025-2026. None of them are in your feed.

---

CHAPTERS

0:00 The Hook — 1,372 People Followed Wrong AI
0:08 The Stakes — 3 Studies You Cannot Self-Detect
0:30 The Offloading Spectrum — Dependent vs Autonomous AI Use
2:30 Cognitive Surrender — Why You Follow Faulty AI
4:30 The Brain Evidence — MIT's EEG Study on LLM Users
6:30 The Theory — Generative Capacity Erosion Hypothesis
8:30 The Moderator — Metacognition Predicts AI Benefit or Harm
10:00 Structural Asymmetry — Why AI Is Different From Calculators
11:30 The Payoff — 6 Peer-Reviewed Findings
12:00 Next — The Metacognition Test (Subscribe)

---

SOURCES (all linked)

1. Shaw & Nave (2026) — Cognitive Surrender — https://osf.io/preprints/psyarxiv/yk25n_v1
2. Kosmyna et al., MIT Media Lab (2025) — Your Brain on ChatGPT — https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08872
3. Frontiers in Psychology (2026) — Not all cognitive offloading is equal — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1878629/full
4. Gupta & Shabista, AAAI (2026) — Generative Capacity Erosion Hypothesis — https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI-SS/article/view/42603
5. APA Monitor (2026) — How AI is reshaping human skills and thinking — https://www.apa.org/monitor/2026/07-08/ai-job-skills-thinking
6. TIME (2026) — Are We Losing Our Minds to AI? — https://time.com/article/2026/04/30/ai-thinking-cognitive-offloading/
7. Anthropic (2026) — 81k Interviews — https://www.anthropic.com/features/81k-interviews

---

LIMITATIONS NOTED

No longitudinal data. MIT study used ChatGPT specifically. Cognitive surrender tested in lab only. Self-reported offloading modes. No clinical harm evidence.
